## Why This Is Asked
- Tests understanding of namespace-scoped network policies and the allow-by-default model.
- Checks ability to craft precise egress rules and test scenarios.
- Evaluates how to verify traffic patterns in a live cluster.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes NetworkPolicy basics, podSelector, egress rules
- Protocols: TCP/UDP, DNS traffic behavior
- Verification: controlled test pods and curl/dig tests

## Code Example
```yaml
# Deny-all egress by default is achieved by allowing only specific egress in a policy
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-web-egress
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector: {}
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.0.0.25/32
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.0.0.0/16
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 53
```

- How would you adapt this policy for egress to a specific set of namespaces or external CIDRs?
- How would you validate that the policy is enforced in a multi-tenant environment?

questions.explanation:
Why This Is Asked

Tests practical, auditable governance for multi-team clusters beyond image/security gates.

Key Concepts

- Namespace governance with ResourceQuota and LimitRange
- Namespace-scoped RBAC and ServiceAccounts
- Lightweight CI gates using kubectl/yq
- Local validation vs CI parity

Code Example

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
for ns in $(kubectl get ns -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do
  kubectl -n "$ns" get resourcequota >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Missing ResourceQuota in $ns"; exit 1; }
  kubectl -n "$ns" get limitrange >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Missing LimitRange in $ns"; exit 1; }
  for dep in $(kubectl -n "$ns" get deploy -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {/end}'); do
    sa=$(kubectl -n "$ns" get deploy "$dep" -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.serviceAccountName}')
    if [ -z "$sa" ]; then echo "Deployment $dep in $ns uses default SA"; exit 1; fi
    kubectl -n "$ns" get rolebinding | grep -q "$sa" || { echo "Missing RBAC for $sa in $ns"; exit 1; }
  done
done
```

Failing manifest

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: team-a
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: app
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      name: app
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:latest
```

Passing manifest

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: team-a
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: rq
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  hard:
    requests.cpu: "4"
    limits.cpu: "8"
    requests.memory: 8Gi
    limits.memory: 16Gi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: lr
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  limits:
  - max:
      cpu: "4"
      memory: 8Gi
    min:
      cpu: 100m
      memory: 128Mi
    default:
      cpu: 500m
      memory: 512Mi
    defaultRequest:
      cpu: 100m
      memory: 128Mi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: sa-team-a
  namespace: team-a
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: sa-team-a-view
  namespace: team-a
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: sa-team-a
  namespace: team-a
roleRef:
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: view
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: app
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      name: app
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: sa-team-a
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:1.21
```

Verification

- Locally: run the gate script against your cluster context and verify it fails/passes as expected; inspect output for missing quota/limitrange or RBAC gaps.
- CI: run the same script in a workflow step; ensure failing manifests fail the build and passing manifests pass.

```javascript
# ConstraintTemplate.sample
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8ssecurity
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sSecurityConstraint
      validation: # omit for brevity
  targets:
  - target: AdmissionReview
    rego: |
      package k8ssecurity
      ...
```
```javascript
# Constraint.sample
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sSecurityConstraint
metadata:
  name: require-secure-images
spec:
  match:
    kinds: [{apiGroups: ["apps"], kinds: ["Deployment"]}]
  parameters: {registry: "registry.example.com/secure/*"}
```
```javascript
# Compliant Pod/Deployment manifest (snippet)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: compliant-app
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: registry.example.com/secure/app:1.0.0
        imagePullPolicy: Always
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 1000
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet: {path: /health, port: 8080}
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet: {path: /health, port: 8080}
        volumeMounts: []
        resources: {requests: {cpu: "100m", memory: "128Mi"}, limits: {cpu: "500m", memory: "256Mi"}}
        readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question probes practical policy design at scale, focusing on admission controls, RBAC hygiene, and network isolation in a multi-cloud Kubernetes environment. It tests how a candidate translates security requirements into Gatekeeper constraints and integrates them into CI.

## Key Concepts
- Open Policy Agent (OPA) Gatekeeper constraint templates
- Kubernetes security: runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, privilege constraints
- RBAC hardening: disallow cluster-admin bindings, namespace-label exceptions
- NetworkPolicy defaults and whitelisting
- CI integration: manifest validation, test manifests, failing/passing samples

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate: noPrivileged
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8snopriv
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sNoPriv
  targets:
  - target: AdmissionReview
    rego: |
      package k8snopriv
      violation["privileged container"] {
        input.review.object.spec.containers[_].securityContext.privileged == true
      }
```

```yaml
# Constraint
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sNoPriv
metadata:
  name: no-privileged-containers
spec:
  enforcementAction: deny
```

## Why This Is Asked

In production Kubernetes environments, ensuring supply-chain security for Helm-based deployments is critical. This question evaluates your ability to integrate multiple security tools—Helm templating, SBOM generation, and image signature verification—into a cohesive CI gate. It tests practical knowledge of enforcing provenance and attestations before code merges.

## Key Concepts

- **Helm templating and values extraction**: Rendering charts to discover all container images referenced in deployments
- **SBOM generation**: Using Syft to create a CycloneDX SBOM that catalogs all dependencies and artifacts
- **Image signing verification**: Using cosign to validate container image signatures against a public key stored in the repository
- **CI gate integration**: Implementing fail-fast behavior in GitHub Actions to block unsigned images and missing attestations

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal GitHub Actions workflow for Helm image signing enforcement
name: Helm Image Security Gate

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  helm-security:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3

      - name: Install Helm and Syft
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/helm/helm/main/scripts/get-helm-3 | bash
          curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anchore/syft/main/install.sh | sh

      - name: Render Helm templates
        run: helm template my-app ./chart --values values.yaml --output-dir ./rendered

      - name: Extract image references
        run: |
          grep -rh 'image:' ./rendered | awk '{print $2}' > images.txt

      - name: Generate SBOM with Syft
        run: |
          syft $(cat images.txt) -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json

      - name: Verify image signatures with cosign
        run: |
          COSIGN_PUBLIC_KEY=cosign.pub
          for IMAGE in $(cat images.txt); do
            cosign verify --key $COSIGN_PUBLIC_KEY $IMAGE || exit 1
          done
```
